decisions.issues: Minor only: a lit brass oil lamp stands in the lower-left foreground of a daylight building site (harmless, open wick, period-correct). Otherwise on beat: laterite bastion with lashed bamboo scaffolding, labourers hauling blocks up an earth ramp, bare-chested Nair musketeers in white mundu and topknots with muskets shouldered, no coats or hats, flat bright sea with no sail. No text. Both captions fit in the open sky at upper right.

Clean. Yusuf reads correctly: lean, white skullcap, neatly trimmed dark beard, dark short sea coat over a white tunic, no turban, no scar, so he is distinct from Ibrahim. He leans over a table piled with cloth, half-smiling, eyes sliding to the side. The market has palm-thatch awnings, open pepper sacks and a brass scale with coins in one pan. Hands are sound. A temple tower in the far background is plausible for south Travancore. Caption space: the thatch band at top left and the sky patch at top right.

Clean. The priest matches the V13 temple-priest sheet: curly hair, white forehead lines with a red dot, sacred thread, gold-bordered white cloth, and an unreadable downcast face. The stout merchant in fine bordered cloth bows low and drops a single silver coin into the brass offering tray. Brass oil-lamp stands light a mandapam at dusk. Hands are sound. The caption fits in the dusk sky at upper left.

Acceptable, with small flaws. On Nagoji's inner left forearm the brand is a tiny dark reddish rosette rather than a pale puckered patch. It is not legible and not a cross, and the long white scar is correct. A faint grey jaw shadow shows, but he reads as clean-shaven. The palm leaf carries a few faint stylus scratches that will not read at print size. Everything else is on lock: black topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, plain cream mundu with no gold border and a shoulder cloth, ivory-handled knife at the waist, NO silver chain. Ramayyan matches his sheet and sits cross-legged among palm-leaf bundles with his stylus, under morning light through a wooden lattice. Ramayyan's balloons fit on the plain wall at upper centre between the doorway and the lattice.

Minor only. The longboat sits in the surf rather than fully run up on the sand, and its plain white pennant flies from the left (bow) end. A tiny distant sail on the horizon is plausibly the envoys' ship. The interpreter (empty-handed, coloured-border shoulder cloth) walks beside the envoys; 1.5 does not name him, but he matches the chapter bible row and 3.2. Envoys are on lock: the senior in a grey powdered wig and charcoal coat with his tricorne at his chest; the younger with his own tied-back brown hair, a brown coat and his tricorne in hand. The scribes are bareheaded clerks in grey coats wading with ribbon-tied paper bundles. No blue coats, soldiers or drums, and the bastion matches 1.1. The caption fits in the open sky at upper left.

v02 is the only candidate offered, and it fixes the round-1 failure: the Dutch party now appears only at the far doorway. Everything the beat needs is there. Varma sits on the low platform in the court look (turban with peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, spear within reach, bare feet on the mat). Nagoji is the only man standing beside the platform, on the king's right, and matches his look: black topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, heavy silver chain with a round pendant, an ivory-handled knife at the waist of a plain cream mundu with no gold border, and a shoulder cloth. Ramayyan sits at the foot of the platform with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Padmini (with her stick) and Revathi (indigo, jasmine braid, armlets, no tali) sit on the left, and ministers sit on both sides. There is no painted text. The top-left rafters and sky, and the top-right rafters, leave room for both captions. Minor, all tolerable: (1) the grey streak at Nagoji's temple is a little stronger than 'a first touch'; (2) the doorway figures are hazy rather than fully featureless, and one of them wears his tricorne on his head; (3) Nagoji's lowered left hand is hidden behind Ramayyan's head, which makes a slight tangent; (4) Padmini's hair shows no grey threading.

Minor issues; acceptable. The shoulder cloth carries a gold stripe, where the script stresses plain cream with no gold border. The chain is drawn as linked oval plaques with a conch pendant, while 2.1 and 2.3 show plain heavy links with a round pendant, so it varies across the page. Otherwise the beat is correct: a heavy silver chain across the cream shoulder cloth, the ivory hilt with the conch mark at the lower edge, and a clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache and gold ear stud at the top edge. There is no text. Both captions fit on the plain cream cloth at the lower left and the rafters and sky at the upper right.

Minor issues; acceptable. Nagoji's hair has a knot on the crown, but long curly locks still hang down behind it, and the grey at his temple is a little stronger than a 'first touch'. The senior envoy's lace jabot and cuff ruffles are fuller than the 'thin lace' the script asks for. The chain is plain heavy links with a round pendant, not the plaque chain of the 2.2 insert. The beat reads clearly: the wigged, heavy-lidded senior envoy holds his tricorne to his chest and slides his eyes toward Nagoji's chain, and the anxious younger envoy, with his own brown hair tied back and in a brown coat, follows the look. Nagoji is cropped at the right edge with no turban, a moustache, a clean chin and an ear stud. There is no text. The caption fits in the clear sky between the envoy's wig and Nagoji.

v02 is the only candidate offered. The foreground beat is right. Lannoy stands at frame right, seen from behind, and matches his sheet: pale curly hair tied with a black ribbon, no wig, white tunic-coat over a white mundu, European sword with its hilt wrapped in local cloth. Two Nair guards (bare chest, white mundu, sword and round shield) stand at ease beside him. In the aisle, the senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, lace cuff) dips a stiff bow with his tricorne at his chest, and the younger envoy (own brown hair tied back, brown coat, hat in hand) stands open-mouthed. The round-1 background faults are fixed: no crown, no spear-bearer, no women on the platform, Nagoji standing on the king's right, and Padmini and Revathi seated on the left. The open sea side matches 2.1. There is no painted text. The sky and rafters above the envoys (upper left) and the plain back wall above the dais both leave clean room for the two balloons. Small residual background faults, each under about 40 px at frame scale: (1) Varma's face is younger, with only a thin moustache instead of the V13 thick curled one; (2) the bald man at the foot of the platform (Ramayyan's place) has a moustache and no curly hair at the sides; (3) Nagoji has a tiny white forehead dot, a gold border on his mundu and shoulder cloth (2.1 shows them plain), a pendant-style silver collar instead of the 2.1 chain, and an earring that reads as a tiny drop. These are candidates for retouching, not grounds for another regeneration.

Minor issues; acceptable. The framing is a waist-up medium shot rather than a tight close-up, and his eyeline goes off screen right. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, no wig, a white tunic-coat over an open-collared shirt and the cloth-wrapped sword hilt. He stands calm and unreadable at a carved pillar at the hall's edge, which matches the blocking, in the same open coastal hall as 2.3 and 2.4. There is no text. Both balloons fit in the open rafters and sky on the left half.

Acceptable with minor deviations. The beat reads clearly: Lannoy in his white tunic-coat, white mundu and sandals, pale hair tied with a black ribbon, steps out at frame right. The senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, tricorne in hand), the younger envoy (brown hair, brown coat), the bareheaded grey-coated scribes and the interpreter (red-and-gold-bordered shoulder cloth) all face the platform. Varma sits still in the turban with the peacock-feather crest, eyes narrowed. Hall blocking matches pages 2 to 7: Nagoji is the only man standing, on the king's right, with a topknot, no turban, a silver chain, the ivory knife, a curled moustache, a clean chin and a gold ear ornament. Ramayyan sits at the foot of the platform, bald crown, clean-shaven, with leaves and stylus. Padmini and Revathi (indigo, jasmine) sit at the left, and the ministers sit at the right. There is no text, no gore and hands are sound. Minor points: Nagoji's grey temple streak is a little heavier than a first touch, though it matches the page-2 candidates. His mundu and shoulder cloth have gold borders, where the script asks for plain cloth. He wears gold armlets. Lannoy's sword hilt is bare gilt instead of wrapped in cloth. Two ministers wear gold chains. No spear is visible near Varma. The long caption fits the low-detail roof and rafter band across the top (y 0 to 0.09), or the top-left corner over the carved pillar, without covering a face.

Minor only. The two scribes write with thin pens on hand-held writing boards, which the script does not ask for but which is harmless and of the period. The senior envoy's lace cuffs are a little fuller than the 'thin trim' of 1.5. Otherwise it is clean: he bows with the tricorne pressed to his chest, and the empty-handed young interpreter in a coloured-border shoulder cloth leans in to relay. The hall, lamps and sea view match 2.1 to 2.4 and 3.1. The roof band and the sky at upper right hold the single balloon.

Minor only. A soft-focus tower building on the far shore at right reads faintly European; it can pass for a coastal bastion. Varma matches the varma-v1 sheet and the ch18 court look: cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, cream and gold cloth, gold necklaces and the spear at hand. His head is tilted and a hand rests on his knee, and both hands are sound. The large clear sky at centre takes all three balloons.

Minor only. The envoy spreads one hand palm-up while the other keeps the tricorne at his chest, not both hands. The grey-coated, bareheaded scribes clutch red-ribbon-tied paper bundles, the younger envoy and the interpreter match 3.2, and the hands and anatomy are sound. The roof band and the open sky between the centre and right pillars give room for the balloons. Ramayyan is off-panel at the platform foot, toward the right where the envoy gestures, so his tail goes to the lower right edge.

Minor. Padmini stands by a pillar, but the hall blocking has her seated with Revathi on the left and 4.5 has them seated. The grey threading the ch16 to 27 row asks for shows only faintly in her hair. The younger envoy's brown coat has gold edging that 3.4 does not show. Padmini otherwise matches her sheet (face, black hair coiled at the nape, gold earrings and necklace, cream sari with gold border in the old drape, long stick) with both hands folded on the stick head. The small background envoy beckons a scribe forward, and the hall and sea match the page. The roof band and the sky at centre and right hold the four balloons.

Minor only. The Dutch scribe offers the ribbon-tied document with one visible hand, not both. The young scribe holds a small bound stack of blank leaves rather than a single palm leaf, though it still reads as a palm-leaf bundle with stylus. Otherwise clean: Ramayyan matches his sheet and lifts two fingers without reaching; the senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, tricorne), younger envoy (brown hair, brown coat), grey-coated bareheaded scribe and empty-handed interpreter all match the ch18 row; same open coastal hall with sea view as pages 2 and 3; no text. 'Read.' fits in the sky between the pillar and the palms or on the mat floor.

Minor staging inconsistency: the envoys, scribe and interpreter sit cross-legged on the mats here, while in 4.1 and 4.4 they stand. Seated envoys already appear in 2.1, and the seated scribe matches 4.3, so this is acceptable. Revathi matches her sheet and the script (profile, indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, bell earrings, sandalwood line, no tali). The paper shows only faint unreadable strokes. The senior envoy's sideways, tight-jawed look at her fits the beat. The caption fits along the dark rafters at the top. Revathi's two balloons fit in the sky and rafters between her head and the senior envoy, above the scribe.

Clean. Lannoy matches the v15b sheet and the ch16-23 row: pale curly hair tied back with a black ribbon, white stand-collar tunic-coat, cloth-wrapped sword hilt as in 2.4. He leans at the pillar with his arms folded (hands sound) and one corner of his mouth twitches. The scribe reads in the soft background, seated as in 4.2. The scribe's off line fits in the large open sky to the upper left. The tail point is the visible background scribe's mouth.

Minor only: Nagoji's grey at the temple is a visible streak rather than a faint first touch; the angle on Varma is closer to eye level than a true low angle and his forward lean is slight; frame is landscape rather than tall. Otherwise clean: Nagoji at the king's right (viewer's left) with black topknot, no turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; Varma in cream-and-gold turban with peacock crest and spear upright; senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, tricorne in hand) back to us in the foreground with the younger envoy and interpreter; ministers murmuring on both sides; same open coastal hall as 4.1-4.3. No painted text. Lettering space: sky above and right of Varma's turban for Varma's lines, and the low-detail charcoal coat back (or sky) for the envoy's line.

Minor only. The senior envoy matches the ch18 lock (grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, black tricorne) and looks down at the hat as scripted. The younger envoy, the grey-coated scribes and the interpreter in his coloured-border cloth are all correct, and the hall matches page 4 (carved pillars, brass lamps, open to the sea). The scribes' pens are dark and cylindrical, a little like modern pens, but they are tiny at print size. Their notebooks show no writing. The open sky at upper right gives clean space for the two envoy balloons and Padmini's small off-panel balloon. Her tail points to the right edge, because in 5.3 she and Revathi sit on the envoys' left, the sea side of the hall.

Minor only. The envoy turns the tricorne idly in his fingers with a casual, heavy-lidded look off to the side, which fits the beat. His costume, the hall and the lighting match 5.1. The interpreter's hair is tied back here but loose in 5.1, a small inconsistency. The scribes' notebooks show no writing. The envoy balloons can sit in the sky gap between the centre pillars, above the ships, or along the roof band at the top.

Minor only. This is one widescreen frame in depth, as scripted. Ramayyan's stylus is stopped on his palm-leaf bundle, though it touches the bundle's top edge rather than an open leaf. His face is also in frame and matches his sheet (receding curly hair, white cloth). Revathi's hand curls into a loose fist on her knee; her indigo-and-gold sari, armlet, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace and sandal line are correct, and she wears no tali. Varma, on the far platform, frowns with narrowed eyes in the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock-feather crest. The red throne hangings behind him do not appear in 4.4 or 5.4, a small setting inconsistency. The caption fits on the plain cream wall above Varma's turban (top centre-right) or on the floor mats at bottom centre. The leaves show no writing.

Acceptable with background quibbles. The two-shot works: the envoy is near with his back half to us (wig, black bow, charcoal coat, tricorne), and Varma sits far and small on the platform, correctly turbaned and crested. The court is silent. The scribe's paper shows no writing. Two background points. Two court women by the dais wear red and green saris; they cannot be mistaken for Revathi (indigo) or Padmini (cream), but they are extra figures. A guard at the far right edge wears a dark vest over a white shirt instead of the bare-chested Nair look, but he is small and cut by the frame. Nagoji, who stood beside the king in 4.4, is not on the platform; the script does not require him here. The envoy balloons can sit in the sky at upper left; Varma's fits on the plain cream wall above his head (about x 0.57 to 0.77, y 0.22 to 0.33). The envoy's face is turned away, so his tail goes to the side of his head.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the ch18 Ananthan Pillai lock: black topknot, no turban, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream shoulder cloth and silver chain. His eyes are turned aside and distant. At full zoom there is light hatched shading on the chin, but it reads as clean-shaven with no beard. The grey streak at the temple is a little more prominent than 'first touch'. The soft-edged inset shows a palm leaf at a raking angle with fine, illegible incised rows, as the script asks, and the small notch at the leaf's edge is clearly the focus. There are no legible letters. The three captions fit along the top-left band over the ceiling and pillars, in the gap between his head and the inset, or on the floor at bottom left, all clear of the face and the notch. The setting matches the hall in the rest of the page.

Minor only. All four fixes from round 1 landed. The red runner and steps carry only plain woven stripes, with no glyphs. Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth are plain cream with no gold border. His arms are clasped behind his back, so the inner left forearm is hidden. The inset shows Revathi's hand relaxed with the fingers open (gold armlet, bangles, indigo-and-gold border), so the fist reads as loosening. Varma matches varma-v1: cream-and-gold turban, jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, spear upright. Nagoji is at the king's right with a topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a gold ear stud and the ivory-handled knife. Remaining quibbles: (1) the grey at Nagoji's temple runs back along the side of his head, more than a 'first touch', as already accepted in 2.3; (2) his chain of office is drawn as a jewelled silver necklace, as accepted in 2.2; (3) he is a heavily muscled figure rather than lean. The envoys' costumes are correct (grey wig and charcoal coat, own brown hair and brown coat), the tricorne is held in hand, the lamp flames stand straight, and the hall is the open-sided carved-pillar hall. Lettering space for the three Varma lines is the rafters at the top right and the large dark backs of the two envoys at the bottom.

Clean. The beat reads: Varma, seen from behind, raises his right hand palm out in the foreground (back of the hand to camera, thumb and four fingers sound), and the senior envoy has his mouth open mid-word. Varma matches his sheet (turban and peacock crest, pearl ear drops, curled moustache, bare back, gold-bordered cloth). The envoys, scribes and interpreter match the chapter 18 row. The room is the same open-sided hall with the sea beyond. Varma's mouth is hidden behind his cheek, so the tail point is at the moustache. There is wide, clear sky across the upper right for all three Varma balloons.

Acceptable, with minor deviations. Varma is framed medium-close rather than tight. Ramayyan is in sharp focus rather than soft, and his leaf bundle is closed, with the stylus paused above it. Both characters match their sheets: Varma in turban and peacock crest with gold necklaces and the spear; Ramayyan thin, with receding curly hair and plain white cloth, his eyes lifted toward the king. The hall matches the neighbouring panels. The anatomy is sound and there is no text. The open sky between the pillars at upper left takes both Varma balloons clear of the faces.

Acceptable, with one staging inconsistency. The round-1 failures are fixed. No one stands beside the king, so there is no Nagoji lookalike. The guards are far back in white headbands, and the seated ministers are bareheaded in plain white with no gold chains. Varma matches varma-v1 (turban, crest, gold necklaces, bare chest). His head and eyes are turned level to screen right, over the seated envoys toward the far side of the hall, and the senior envoy looks up at him with a clenched jaw and pressed lips. That is the swallow beat, though the jabot hides the throat itself. Remaining issues: (1) both envoys sit cross-legged on the mats, while in 6.2 and 7.1 they stand. A similar seated staging was accepted in 4.2, but readers may notice it on this page. (2) The left scribe writes on a small low writing board, which is close to the 'no tables' rule but harmless. (3) No spear is in reach, which this panel does not require. Envoy costumes are correct, the hall and lighting match 6.2, and the broad clear sky across the upper middle takes both balloons without touching a face.

Minor only. The round-1 failure is fixed: this is now a strip about Lannoy alone, with no platform, king, women, ministers or guards. Lannoy matches the v15b sheet and the ch16-23 row: pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, no wig, white stand-collar tunic-coat, white mundu. He stands very straight against a carved tiger pillar on a laterite base at screen right. In the soft foreground at left, only the backs of the envoys show, in the correct locks: the senior's grey wig with black bow and charcoal coat, and the younger's own brown hair tied back with a brown coat. Remaining quibbles: (1) Lannoy's eyes go off to screen right, away from the envoys rather than 'past their shoulders', though it still reads as a fixed refusal to meet them; (2) the sword hilt is brass with a cloth knotted around it rather than a fully wrapped grip, and it hangs with no visible belt, as accepted in 7.1. The hall, brass open-wick lamps, sea view and daylight match 6.4. Both off-panel Varma balloons fit in the clear sky in the upper middle. Their tails run to the left frame edge, toward the platform side established in 6.4.

Minor only: Lannoy's hilt is brass with a knotted cloth tassel rather than a fully wrapped grip, and the scabbard hangs without a visible belt. Ramayyan, both envoys (tricornes held to the chest, the younger one looking as if he might choke, the senior one composed), Lannoy at his pillar in white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, and the open-sided hall all match pages 2 to 6. Lettering space: the roof and rafter band at upper left, above Ramayyan, is clear.

Clean. The Dutch paper lies flat beside the tied palm-leaf bundle and stylus. It carries only faint blurred rows with nothing legible, as the script asks. Ramayyan is seated, calm, below the standing senior envoy. Lettering space: the open sky between the pillars at left and centre-left, and the roof band at top right.

Minor only: the hall behind him reads empty in this close shot, with a plain back wall at right that does not appear in earlier panels. It is plausible for this camera angle. Ramayyan matches his sheet and is writing on his leaf, with his forearm pinning the Dutch paper at the left edge. The paper's marks are faint and illegible. Hands are sound. The plain wall at right gives generous space for the three heavy balloons.

Acceptable. Small notes only. The golden late-afternoon light reads as 'later', but 7.1, 7.3 and 7.5 are in blue-sky daylight, so 7.5 jumps back to midday right after this panel. The cloth on Lannoy's sword hilt is red here and white in 7.5, and no belt is visible holding the scabbard. Everything else matches: Lannoy fits his sheet (pale hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, ankle-length mundu, sandals, hands clasped behind his back) and stands by a carved pillar at frame right. The senior envoy has his grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, thin lace cuffs and tricorne at his chest, and has stopped beside Lannoy, centre-left. Bare-chested Nair guards with sword and round shield lead the younger envoy (brown coat, his own hair), two grey-coated scribes and the interpreter toward frame left. Background chiefs walk off in pairs and the platform is empty. It is the same open coastal hall seen in the neighbouring panels. I found no text (the scribe's book is blank), no blood and no anachronism, and the hands are sound. Clear sky between the pillars, above both heads, has room for the envoy's balloon (upper centre-left) and Lannoy's (upper centre-right) without covering a face.

Minor only. The sky is a pale late-day blue, not the pinkish sunset of 7.4; this is acceptable, and the 7.4 regeneration is asked for matching late-afternoon light. The sword hilt here is fully cloth-wrapped, while 7.1 and 7.4 show a brass grip with a cloth knot. The script beat is met: a close two-shot in profile, the two men facing away from each other. The envoy has his grey wig, charcoal coat and thin lace cuff. Lannoy has his own pale hair tied back, the white tunic-coat and the cloth-wrapped hilt at his hip. Lettering space: the rafter band across the top and the sky and palms between the two heads.

Minor only. A thin gold hem shows on the trailing end of Nagoji's shoulder cloth, but the mundu itself is plain, so it barely touches the chapter's no-gold-border lock. The grey at his temple is one bold streak, a little more than a first touch, but the hair is clearly black and he is not the grey later-life figure. The rest matches: topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, silver chain catching the light, conch-marked ivory knife. Revathi is in indigo with jasmine braid, flat coins, armlets and sandalwood line; her tiny brow dot matches her sheet. The verandah, palms, sea and low sun are right. The open sky at upper right, and the roof beams above the post, take the short balloon.

Clean apart from the flat coins catching the light only modestly, not as bright small suns. Revathi is half-turned to camera at the rail on the same verandah and in the same light as 8.1, Nagoji is not drawn, and her hands and bangles are sound. The whole sky and sea on the right half are clear for the four balloons. Nagoji's off-panel tail goes to the left edge, the direction he is coming from along the verandah.

Clean. The framing now matches the beat: a tight insert from Nagoji's point of view on Revathi's throat. Flat gold coin discs, not round beads, fill the centre and catch the low sun. Only her lips and jaw show at the top edge, with no eyes and no repeat of the 8.2 portrait. The jasmine braid, jhumka and gold armlet match 8.2. The sari is indigo with a gold border and there is no tali. The verandah post, rail, palms and sunset sea are in the same light as 8.2. The face entry covers only her partial lower face (mouth and jaw), so the caption is kept off it. The warm sky above the sea at upper right, about x 0.68 to 1.0 and y 0.02 to 0.22, is clear for the one caption.

The r1 failures are fixed. Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth are now plain cream with no gold border. His chain is now a round-link silver chain with a small round pendant. Minor issues remain, none disqualifying. The brand on his inner left forearm is a small brownish ring or rosette-like mark, placed mid-forearm nearer the elbow, next to the long white scar. It is a little more defined than a shapeless patch, but it is tiny at panel scale, has no letters and is not a cross. The chain is lighter than the heavier silver chain in 8.1. Padmini shows somewhat more grey than 'a few threads', but her hair is still mostly black and coiled at the nape. Everything else matches. Padmini walks in from frame left with her long stick, in a cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse. Nagoji has a black topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a small gold stud and the ivory knife at his waist, with his left hand on the rail. Revathi wears indigo with flat coins, jasmine braid, armlets and bangles. It is the same verandah and sunset as 8.1 to 8.3. All hands are sound. Balloon space: Padmini's medium balloon fits over the roof eaves at top left, and Nagoji's and Revathi's short balloons fit in the open sky at top centre and right.

Clean. The r1 failure is fixed. The brand is now a pale, shiny, puckered patch of raised ridges just above the wrist, with no shape, symbol, letters or cross. The long thin white scar runs from it toward the elbow. The cloth at frame right is plain cream with no gold edge. Revathi's bangled hand enters from frame left, and her fingertips brush the back of Nagoji's hand on the rail. His hand reads as a LEFT hand: back of the hand up, four fingers over the rail edge, thumb tucked on the far side. His nails are darkened and slightly ridged. A fold of gold-patterned indigo sari sits at frame left. Finger counts and anatomy are sound, and there is no pseudo-text. The verandah post, rail and sunset sea match 8.4. The open sky across the top is clear for both captions.

Minor: Padmini's hair carries somewhat more grey than the 'mostly black, a few threads of grey' line, but it still reads as dark hair coiled at the nape, so it passes. Everything else is clean. Nagoji has a black topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small flush gold stud, a silver chain and the ivory knife at his waist. Revathi has the sandalwood line, no red dot, the flat-coin necklace, jasmine and armlets. The verandah at sunset with a timber rail matches 9.1 and 9.3. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. The open sky across the top center and top right gives room for Revathi's long balloon and Nagoji's short one.

Minor issue: the silver chain on Nagoji in the foreground is a plain beaded chain, not the plaque-link chain of office seen in 8.x, but only a short length shows. Otherwise clean. Revathi matches her sheet (blouse, coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, jasmine braid). In the foreground Nagoji has the black topknot with the same touch of grey as page 8, a flush gold ear stud, the moustache tip, a cream shoulder cloth and no turban. Hands are sound, and the upper-right sky leaves plenty of room for both balloons.

Clean. Nagoji has a black topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small gold stud and the silver chain of office on his chest. He sits cross-legged at a low writing board with a reed pen, a small brass ink pot and a clay open-wick lamp on a brass tray, which matches 9.5. The papers show only faint strokes, not legible text. His large shadow falls on the limewashed wall, and the shuttered window looks out on dark hills. The dark upper wall around the shadow is clear for the two captions.
